title: GET /api/portfolio — non-blocking review follow-ups
description: Non-blocking findings from pr-reviewer's review of PR #30 (api-portfolio-get), tracked here per CLAUDE.md's autonomous-pipeline rule so they aren't lost once that PR merges.

checklist.step: The mark-to-market enrichment logic (fetch current_price per position via the DataProvider, compute unrealized_pnl_pct, sum positions_value, exclude a position whose price fetch failed) is embedded directly in app/api/routers/portfolio.py's get_portfolio handler using the API schema types, rather than as a reusable function in app/portfolio/ built on the existing app.portfolio.models.Position/Equity/Account domain models (which already have the exact shape for this). The still-stubbed GET /api/portfolio/risk endpoint (api-portfolio-risk task) needs position.current_price populated too (per app/portfolio/risk.py's precondition), so as currently structured it will have to duplicate this same fetch-and-degrade-gracefully loop instead of reusing it. Extract into a portfolio-domain function both routes can call.

docs/architecture/Backend.md §2's module layout diagram doesn't list the new app/api/dependencies.py file added by this PR. Not a violation of any documented principle (it fits the existing api/ layer and the get_db dependency-override testing pattern), but the diagram should be updated for accuracy.

get_portfolio's db.query(PositionORM).all() has no explicit order_by, so the order of `positions` in the response isn't deterministic/guaranteed -- it currently relies on incidental SQLite behavior. Low impact for a single-user MVP but worth an explicit stable ordering (e.g. by entry_date or id) for a deterministic API response.

get_portfolio's db session and get_data_provider's CachedDataProvider share the same request-scoped SQLAlchemy Session (default expire_on_commit=True, app/db/session.py's sessionmaker doesn't override it). A cache-miss/stale price fetch mid-loop commits (CachedDataProvider._upsert) on that same session, expiring every already-loaded PositionORM object, so each subsequent row attribute access re-issues a SELECT -- an N+1 query pattern for a portfolio with a cold cache. Not a correctness bug, just wasteful; consider passing expire_on_commit=False for this session or loading all needed row attributes before the fetch loop.

The account=None -> cash=0.0 fallback in get_portfolio (no AccountORM row exists for a fresh DB, since nothing seeds account id=1) is a real judgment call not pinned down by docs/architecture/API.md, but wasn't recorded in api-portfolio-get's decisions array per CLAUDE.md's decision-memory section. Record it (or revisit whether a missing account row should instead be treated as a seed-data bug / 500).

get_portfolio's per-position price fetches (_latest_close in the for-loop) run strictly sequentially in a synchronous handler, so total request latency scales linearly with position count on any cache miss -- a single slow/rate-limited upstream call stalls every position behind it. The DataProvider protocol has no batch method today, so this would need a protocol change or a concurrency wrapper to fix.

decisions.decision: Checklist item 1 (extract the mark-to-market enrichment loop into a reusable app/portfolio/ function) is already satisfied -- no code change made for it in this task. The api-portfolio-risk task (PR #33, merged ahead of this task being picked up) performed exactly this extraction, creating app/portfolio/pricing.py (EnrichedPosition/enrich_positions_with_price/positions_value) and refactoring GET /api/portfolio's handler to use it alongside GET /api/portfolio/risk, per that task's own decisions entry.
decisions.rationale: Verified directly against the current codebase (not just the other task's decisions entry) before marking this done: app/portfolio/pricing.py exists, both get_portfolio and get_risk in app/api/routers/portfolio.py call enrich_positions_with_price/positions_value from it, and docs/architecture/Backend.md §6 already documents the module. Redoing the extraction here would either be a no-op or, worse, risk diverging from the already-reviewed and merged implementation in pricing.py. This task's instructions explicitly anticipated this ordering (api-portfolio-risk could land first) and called for checking before acting rather than blindly redoing the work.

decisions.decision: Ordered both get_portfolio's and get_risk's position query by (entry_date, id) via a new shared `_ordered_positions(db)` helper in app/api/routers/portfolio.py, rather than by id alone.
decisions.rationale: The checklist item's own suggestion ('e.g. by entry_date or id') left the choice open. entry_date matches how a user conceptually thinks of their portfolio (positions listed in the order they were established), which id -- an opaque `pos_<uuid hex>` string with no chronological meaning (see api-portfolio-add-position's id-generation) -- doesn't provide; ordering by id alone would produce a stable but semantically arbitrary sequence. id is kept as the tiebreaker for two positions sharing the same entry_date, since entry_date alone isn't unique and SQL ORDER BY needs a fully deterministic key to guarantee stability across engines/executions. Applied the same helper to GET /api/portfolio/risk's equivalent query too (not explicitly named in this checklist item, but sharing the identical `db.query(PositionORM).all()` pattern) for consistency -- leaving one endpoint deterministic and the other not would be a strange half-fix for what is the same underlying gap. Covered by a new integration test in both tests/integration/test_portfolio_get.py and tests/integration/test_portfolio_risk.py that inserts positions out of both entry_date and id order and asserts the response reflects the expected sort, not insertion order.

decisions.decision: Fixed the N+1 query pattern by setting expire_on_commit=False on app/db/session.py's production `SessionLocal`, rather than the checklist item's other suggested option (loading all needed row attributes before the fetch loop).
decisions.rationale: expire_on_commit=False is a one-line, request-session-wide fix that addresses the root cause (CachedDataProvider._upsert's mid-loop commit expiring every loaded object on the shared session) rather than a narrower workaround scoped to just the portfolio-positions loop; it also covers any future caller that shares a session with CachedDataProvider the same way, not just today's two routes. The alternative -- eagerly reading every row's needed attributes into plain values before the fetch loop begins -- was rejected as more invasive (it would mean enrich_positions_with_price/pricing.py working over detached plain data instead of live PositionORM rows, or the router pre-extracting fields itself) for a problem this session-level fix already solves cleanly. Confirmed safe for the codebase's other session users: the only other `db.commit()` call sites (add_position, delete_position in app/api/routers/portfolio.py) either explicitly call db.refresh(row) afterward (which always re-fetches regardless of expire_on_commit, per SQLAlchemy's docs) or don't touch the committed row's attributes again in the same request, so expire_on_commit=False changes no other route's observed behavior. Added tests/unit/test_db_session.py::test_session_local_does_not_expire_objects_on_commit (asserts the config directly) and tests/integration/test_portfolio_pricing_session.py (a behavioral regression test: counts SQL SELECTs issued against the positions table across a two-position enrichment loop with a real mid-loop cache commit, asserting zero re-selects with the fix's config and a companion test confirming the same technique reproduces >0 re-selects under the old expire_on_commit=True default, so the fix is verified to actually change the outcome, not just the config value in isolation).

decisions.decision: Recorded the account=None -> cash=0.0 fallback as a decisions entry directly on docs/tasks/api-portfolio-get.json (the task the checklist item pointed at), rather than revisiting it as a seed-data bug / 500 in this task.
decisions.rationale: See the new entry on that task for the full rationale: in short, no AccountORM(id=1) row existing is a seed-data gap that db-migrations is expected to close (an always-present seeded account row), not a per-request error condition worth a 404/422/500 today, and the existing empty-portfolio test fixture already relies on 'no account row' and 'a genuinely empty portfolio' being indistinguishable at this layer -- changing that now would be a behavior change out of this followups task's non-blocking scope, not just a documentation gap.

decisions.decision: Left the sequential per-position price-fetch latency as a documented known limitation (this entry) rather than a code fix.
decisions.rationale: The DataProvider protocol (app/data/base.py) has no batch method, and neither YFinanceProvider nor StooqProvider's underlying libraries (yfinance's per-ticker Ticker API as used here, Stooq's per-ticker CSV endpoint) are wrapped in this codebase in a way that supports a genuine batched fetch today -- adding one would be a protocol change touching every DataProvider implementation and CachedDataProvider's cache-key granularity (per-ticker rows), well beyond a non-blocking follow-up's scope. A concurrency wrapper (e.g. a thread pool around the existing per-ticker calls in enrich_positions_with_price) was considered and rejected for now: CachedDataProvider shares a single SQLAlchemy Session (app/db/session.py) across all its cache reads/writes, and SQLAlchemy Sessions are not thread-safe for concurrent use from multiple threads at once -- parallelizing the fetch loop as it's currently structured would introduce a real correctness bug (concurrent session access) to fix a performance one, which is a worse trade for a single-user MVP where portfolios are expected to be small. This is genuinely a scale limitation worth revisiting if/when either the DataProvider protocol grows batch support or the session-per-request pattern changes (e.g. a session-per-fetch design), not something with a straightforward fix available today.
